title: Zakaria Khan’s Proclamation Deepens the Anti-Sikh Terror

blocks.text: Zakaria Khan’s proclamation turns the persecution of the Sikhs into a wider social campaign. Villagers are pressured to inform, those who shelter Singhs risk destruction, and whole districts become unsafe as fear and greed begin serving the Nawab’s policy.

The result is another scattering of the Khalsa. Some flee into forests, hills, and distant courts, while others survive by concealment and mobility because normal village life has been poisoned by surveillance and bounty seeking.

Within that crisis the narrative points toward Mehtab Singh’s exile and grief. Even from Jaipur he continues hearing of Punjab’s misery, which prepares the moral ground for direct action against sacrilege and oppression.
